title: ddmo: A Compatible PySINDy Engine for Feature Optimization in Sparse Dynamical-System Discovery
abstractExcerpt: Sparse equation discovery depends on the candidate functions, the treatment of noisy data, and the sparse regression procedure. These components are commonly configured independently, although their interactions directly affect model recovery. Our data-driven model optimizer ddmo uses PySINDy as its default sparse-regression backend and adds a modular, multiobjective optimization layer around it. Within one configurable search, users can vary parameters of prescribed candidate functions, regression settings, and the test functions and windows used to construct weak-form equations.

title: FusionRCG: Orchestrating Recursive Computation Graphs across GPU Memory Hierarchies

s2.tldr: FusionRCG is presented, a framework that jointly optimizes computation graph structure and GPU memory mapping and contributes liveness-aware graph orchestration to minimize peak live intermediates and an adaptive multi-tier kernel architecture routing graphs across the memory hierarchy.

abstractExcerpt: Evaluating high-dimensional integrals via deep hierarchical recurrences is a dominant cost in quantum chemistry. While CPUs manage these efficiently, GPUs suffer a critical mismatch: limited per-thread memory is quickly overwhelmed by an explosion of simultaneously live intermediate variables. As recurrence scales, this forces massive data spilling to global memory, collapsing performance into a severe memory-bound regime. We present FusionRCG, a framework that jointly optimizes computation graph structure and GPU memory mapping.

abstractExcerpt: Electron microscopy provides direct real-space access to the structural heterogeneity of catalysts across multiple length scales.
